non-technical-founder.who: Has an idea and no engineering background; wants a working, maintained product without touching code, cloud accounts or deploys.

stories.story: I describe my idea by voice and get a live site that keeps itself updated.
I never see a key, a config file or a deploy command; if something needs me it is one link with a default already in effect.

solo-developer-maintainer.who: Maintains open-source or a small product alone; drowning in issues, reviews and releases.

stories.story: New issues are triaged, fixed in a PR, reviewed by a different agent, merged and verified live without me.
A stuck or abandoned agent session never holds work hostage.

research-lab.who: Academic or independent researcher; needs ideas turned into reviewed, versioned, citable publications.

stories.story: A queued idea becomes a reviewed draft and at least two published versions with a citation file.

small-team-startup.who: Two to ten people; cannot hire a marketing, legal, finance or support function yet.

stories.story: Roles I cannot hire exist as agents that wake on schedule and on events, phased in as the code loop proves itself.
Funding applications and outreach run within caps, consent and suppression, with source-checked claims before anything goes public.

platform-governance-lead.who: Responsible for what autonomous agents may do; needs earned trust, budgets and audit.

stories.story: Agents gain autonomy per action class only through verified outcomes, and lose it on a hidden failure.
A breached spend cap steers work to cheaper paths and blocks new workers; it never silently overspends.

objections.objection: Isn't this just a code agent?
objections.answer: A code agent is one component (code-executor). The product is the loop around it: what wakes it, who assigns it work, who reviews it, what verifies the deploy, and how the loops improve themselves.

objections.objection: Claude Code's maker has far more funding; surely they have thought of this.
objections.answer: A model vendor sells the agent; this product is vendor-neutral orchestration on the customer's own repository and cloud, so it routes across vendors rather than competing with one.

objections.objection: Automation tools and workflow engines already trigger things on a schedule.
objections.answer: They trigger steps; they do not own work items with claims, independent review, trust, or self-scoring, and they do not run a business function team.

objections.objection: Is it safe to let agents run unattended?
objections.answer: Autonomy is earned per action class, budgets steer rather than stop, every change is reviewed by a different agent, and an irreversible identity-bound act is a single card with a default in effect.

objections.objection: Can a non-technical person really use this?
objections.answer: The entry point is a spoken idea and a short either/or interview; the generator produces the instance manifest and the cloud setup runs from it.

objections.objection: Does it really run on itself?
objections.answer: Its roadmap, issues, roles, trust ledger and loops are executed by the same kernel it ships, and this gap analysis is computed from probes, not written.

closest_overlaps.why_it_matters: Cloud scheduled tasks with schedule, API and GitHub triggers directly cover the unattended-wake claim.
Automations fire on PRs, CI, Slack, Linear, Sentry and PagerDuty and include autofix, covering much of the wake-and-act loop.
Automatic PR review is native in several products (Claude Code, Codex, Devin, Cursor Bugbot, Copilot, Factory), so review alone is not a moat.
Four trigger types plus built-in triage, QA, incident and CVE automations resemble an autonomous engineering org in product form.
Heartbeats, timeouts and durable history are mature infrastructure for lease and reaper behavior; differentiation must lie in the agent-specific layer.

caveats: Static probes (file, grep) show a connection exists in code; only a component with a passing proof probe (test or live evidence) is called live.
Competitor cells come from doctrine/market-evidence.json with sources and an access date; unknown means not verified, and an unverified cell never counts as support.
Most cells marked unknown mean the specific doc page was not fetched or did not mention the capability; they are not evidence of absence.

Cells marked no for domain components (funding-outreach, ip-legal, research-publishing, marketing-content, customer-onboarding, bootstrap-from-idea, role-managers) rest on feature lists reviewed, not exhaustive proof; a vendor could ship one unannounced.
n8n was not researched; Zapier Agents was used as the automation-platform representative and only its trigger docs were verified.
Many docs pages were summarized by a fetch tool rather than read in full; notes are paraphrases and should be re-checked before quoting to investors.
Several product claims come from secondary sources (dev.to for Copilot assignment, search summaries for Cursor, Devin and Codex); primary-source confirmation is advised.
Products ship fast and some are preview features (Claude Code scheduled tasks are labeled research preview); status is as of 2026-11-12.
The components describe an integrated whole; a product covering each piece natively is not the same as covering the integrated whole, but no product was found that does so.
